**Sundhedsklynge Sydvestjylland** is a regional healthcare cluster operating within [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] [^src3][^src6]. It is one of the local organizational units evaluated in the Danish national clinical quality monitoring program for the treatment of [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] [^src2][^src4]. The cluster's performance is systematically tracked across multiple clinical quality indicators to ensure evidence-based and safe cardiovascular treatment [^src4][^src5].

The cluster is particularly notable in the 2024 quality reports for failing to meet the national benchmark on key treatment metrics. For Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy in newly diagnosed patients, Sundhedsklynge Sydvestjylland recorded a compliance rate of 87.9%, falling short of the required 90% standard [^src1]. Furthermore, it was explicitly identified as one of only four clusters nationwide—alongside [[klynge-syd|Klynge SYD]], [[klynge-nord|Klynge NORD]], and [[goedstrupklyngen|Gødstrupklyngen]]—that did not meet the standard for [[indikator-4a3|Indikator 4a3]], which tracks long-term (5-year) persistence in anticoagulation treatment [^src4]. 

Beyond treatment initiation and persistence, the cluster's patient outcomes and safety metrics are closely monitored. Its data contributes to the national geographic mapping of [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], which tracks the incidence of ischemic stroke (apopleksi) among atrial fibrillation patients [^src5]. The cluster also reports localized statistics on 1-year and 2-year treatment coverage [^src2], annual kidney function monitoring (P-creatinine) for patients on DOACs [^src5], and adverse outcomes such as severe bleeding (Indikator 11) and heart failure (Indikator 15) within the first year of diagnosis [^src7][^src8]. These granular, cluster-level metrics are essential for identifying local variations in clinical practice and guiding targeted quality improvement initiatives across the Danish healthcare system [^src2][^src4].
